content.text: Changing passwords also requires checking new access and informing operators. At scale, tracking which account changed when is challenging.
I changed a test password with Password Provisioning, then connected as a user and ran commands. Managing rotation and access in the same system was convenient.
Choosing the Server and Account
I prepared a separate Ubuntu server and
rotateops
account. Enabling Password Provisioning in Servers → Configurations exposed jobs and account-status management.

attrs.alt: Screen 1. Password Provisioning enabled with account-management menus.
attrs.caption: Screen 1. Password Provisioning enabled with account-management menus.

content.text: A dedicated group contained only this server. I registered the account as
QueryPie - Provisioning
. The saved authentication method was
Managed by Job
, clearly indicating management through password-rotation jobs.

attrs.alt: Screen 2. rotateops registered for password-provisioning management.
attrs.caption: Screen 2. rotateops registered for password-provisioning management.

content.text: Creating a Job for One Server and Account
In Password Provisioning, I created
EP46 Rotate Test Account
for the dedicated group. Target Server 1 and Target Accounts rotateops confirmed scope before execution.
The password-changing account was separate from the login account: an isolated-server administrator performed rotation, while users connected as rotateops. Execution was
Manual

attrs.caption: Screen 3. Target scope verified and job saved for manual execution.

content.text: Checking Results per Account
Run Job finished Completed. History details showed rotateops
Success
. I also verified the password changed on the server itself.

attrs.alt: Screen 4. Target account password change succeeds.
attrs.caption: Screen 4. Target account password change succeeds.

content.text: Account Management listed server, account, purpose, and
Last Password Updated At
, recording this change at 13:16:04. Last-rotation times per account avoid separate manual tracking.

attrs.caption: Screen 5. Last password-change timestamp in account management.

content.text: Connecting Without Entering the New Password
The assigned user role showed rotateops Active. Connect worked without finding and typing the newly changed server password.

attrs.alt: Screen 6. Authorized user connects with managed rotateops.
attrs.caption: Screen 6. Authorized user connects with managed rotateops.

content.text: whoami, hostname, and pwd returned rotateops, acp-ep46-password-lab, and /home/rotateops. Authorized work remained possible after rotation.

attrs.alt: Screen 7. Account and server verified using the updated credentials.
attrs.caption: Screen 7. Account and server verified using the updated credentials.

content.text: The administrator rotates credentials while users continue through assigned QueryPie access, reducing redistribution of each new password.
Password Management and Access History Together
Server Access History showed Demo Developer at 13:17:24 using EP46 Rotation Operator and rotateops, result Success.

attrs.alt: Screen 8. Person, role, and actual server account in the audit.
attrs.caption: Screen 8. Person, role, and actual server account in the audit.

content.text: Rotation was visible in Password Provisioning/Account Management; the person using it was visible in access history, even with a server account shared for work.
One account’s rotation and fresh connection showed a practical combination: password jobs, user access, and history together, with simple user connection steps even under regular password management.
